lesson_title: The Science of Not Enough: What Economics Studies
hook_text: You've been doing economics since your first R50. Nobody told you.
clip_script: Here's a whole school subject in one sentence: everybody wants more than there is — now what? You on a Saturday with R50: airtime, chips, that cap, taxi money. The R50 can't cover it all — and the moment one want is satisfied, another steps forward. That endless queue? Unlimited wants. The R50 — and behind it the world's land, workers, machines — limited resources. Economics is the study of that gap. And every economy, from your pocket to the country, runs the same three-step engine on it: somebody MAKES things — the gogo baking vetkoek is combining resources, labour, capital and risk. People SWAP things — vetkoek for coins at the rank. People USE things — and a want dies happy, until lunchtime, when it's reborn. Make, swap, use. Production, exchange, consumption. The fancy names describe your street perfectly. Welcome to the science of not enough.
visual_style: A R50 note splitting toward a queue of glowing wants that never shortens; then a township street loop animating make→swap→use with the gogo, the rank and the eater in one continuous cycle.
mood: Recognition and delight — school subject meets street life.
pacing: Punchy one-sentence open, rhythmic three-step engine, warm landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and put names to what you already practise.
